workstream: W4-1e — Inventory service, land and infrastructure indicators
scope: Official City Government of Makati, PSA, DepEd and PhilHealth sources only. This step inventories service, land, environmental and physical-infrastructure indicators that can be stated with a defined period/geography. It does not implement indicator data or expand Place Registry coverage.
coreRule: Source-backed inventory counts own the denominator. Place Registry may supply exact relationships to named assets, but its current record count must never be substituted for an official citywide denominator.

officialSources.title: Makati City Basic Facts and Figures 2023
officialSources.geography: 23 barangays for the city profile; the relevant environment, infrastructure, health, public-education and social-welfare measures explicitly note exclusion of the 10 transferred barangays where applicable.
usableFor: day-care and selected social-service facility counts
officialSources.note: Treat these as 2023 administrative snapshots, not timeless/current counts. Several transport and service counts need fresher source confirmation before headline use.

candidateIndicators.definition: Area and percentage share of each official existing land-use category.
candidateIndicators.note: Keep the official category vocabulary. Do not infer parcel-level land use for a Place Registry record from the citywide distribution.

candidateIndicators.definition: Total area represented by the current-boundary 2022 existing-land-use table.
candidateIndicators.note: 18,168,300 sq m. Keep distinct from PSA land-area metadata if definitions/measurement bases differ.

candidateIndicators.definition: Public parks reported by the City Government's environmental-management inventory.
candidateIndicators.note: Official denominator is 15. The Wave 3 civic-audit target currently contains 13 verified public-park records; do not replace the official count with 13 or claim all 15 have canonical Place Registry matches until exact identities are reconciled.

candidateIndicators.definition: Number of trees reported by the Department of Environmental Services.
candidateIndicators.note: Useful environmental snapshot, but stock-count method and refresh cadence are not sufficiently described for trend interpretation.

candidateIndicators.definition: Length of concreted roads reported by the Department of Engineering and Public Works.
candidateIndicators.note: Aggregate city infrastructure measure; do not derive or backfill street-segment status in Place Registry from this total.

candidateIndicators.definition: Length of asphalt roads reported by the Department of Engineering and Public Works.
candidateIndicators.note: Aggregate city infrastructure measure; do not infer segment-by-segment surface type.

candidateIndicators.definition: Length of improved drainage reported by the Department of Engineering and Public Works.
candidateIndicators.note: Use as a dated network total. Individual drainage segments require their own explicit source relationship.

candidateIndicators.definition: Streetlight poles reported by the Department of Engineering and Public Works.
candidateIndicators.note: A point-stock count is useful but needs a fresher inventory before headline publication.

candidateIndicators.definition: Number of bike lanes reported by the Department of Engineering and Public Works.
candidateIndicators.note: The source reports a count of 9 but does not define whether a 'bike lane' means corridor, segment, direction or project. Do not convert this into lane-kilometres.

candidateIndicators.definition: MRT stations reported within Makati.
candidateIndicators.note: Stable-looking infrastructure count, but Mobility/Place Registry should own exact station identities. Statistics may reference that canonical set after explicit reconciliation.

candidateIndicators.definition: PNR stations reported within Makati in the 2023 city inventory.
candidateIndicators.note: A station-location snapshot does not establish current passenger-service availability. Do not present the 2023 count as current transit service.

candidateIndicators.definition: Bus stops reported by the Department of Engineering and Public Works.
candidateIndicators.note: Stop inventories can change with route/traffic schemes. Require a current operational source before headline use.

candidateIndicators.definition: Distinct schools in the DepEd Makati City National Inventory Dashboard.
candidateIndicators.geography: current Schools Division of Makati City
candidateIndicators.note: Do not compare 23 distinct schools to the Basic Facts total of public school 'levels', because the latter counts overlapping program/level categories.

candidateIndicators.definition: School infrastructure projects submitted in DepEd's National Inventory Dashboard.
candidateIndicators.geography: current Schools Division of Makati City
candidateIndicators.note: Useful for an education-infrastructure page or report, but project-submission count is not a service-capacity metric.

candidateIndicators.definition: Health centers reported by the Makati Health Department in the city Basic Facts inventory.
candidateIndicators.note: Keep distinct from PhilHealth accreditation/provider counts. A facility may exist without appearing in the YAKAP/GAMOT list.

candidateIndicators.definition: Makati City providers in PhilHealth's list of accredited YAKAP clinics with available GAMOT prescription.
candidateIndicators.note: Use the provider list itself as the denominator. Exact city-government health-center identities may link to canonical Place Registry health-center records only when IDs resolve exactly.

candidateIndicators.definition: Named City Government of Makati health centers in PhilHealth's YAKAP/GAMOT provider list.
candidateIndicators.note: The list also contains one City Government of Makati entry for Makati Health Department, yielding 17 government entries in total.

candidateIndicators.definition: DOH-licensed Makati health facilities by regulatory facility type.
candidateIndicators.note: Do not hand-count from changing NCR PDFs or dashboards without a reproducible extraction and as-of date.

candidateIndicators.definition: Day-care centers reported by the Makati Social Welfare Department.
candidateIndicators.note: Potential social-service infrastructure indicator, but lower priority than the first Statistics batch and should ideally be refreshed.

candidateIndicators.definition: Stated city processing times for selected transactions in Basic Facts and Figures.
candidateIndicators.note: These are stated processing times/service standards, not measured outcome or compliance performance. Transaction guides/Citizen Charter should own service-standard information.

comparabilityRules: Every facility/network count must carry an as-of/year; city administrative inventories are snapshots, not timeless facts.
A count from Place Registry is never a substitute for a citywide denominator unless an official complete inventory establishes that the registry is complete for that exact indicator.
When an official denominator exceeds exact canonical Place Registry matches, publish the official count and expose the relationship-coverage gap separately rather than lowering the denominator.
Distinct schools, school-level/program counts, classrooms and school infrastructure projects are different measures and must not be combined.
Health-center existence, DOH license, PhilHealth accreditation and YAKAP/GAMOT availability are different states and require separate indicator IDs.
A transport station/stop location count does not establish current route operation or passenger-service availability.
Road length, drainage length, bike-lane count and streetlight stock have different units and cannot be aggregated into a composite infrastructure score.
Land-use percentages must retain their 2022 reference year and current 23-barangay boundary; document publication year does not change the observation year.
Administrative processing-time standards are not observed service-performance metrics.
Missing current facility data remains unavailable; do not carry forward a 2023 count as 'current' without an explicit dated label.

implementationBatchRecommendation.rationale: The first batch combines a current-boundary land-use baseline, source-owned environmental/infrastructure snapshots and two current 2026 service-access inventories. It gives Statistics useful civic context without converting incomplete Place Registry coverage or stale service standards into invented current metrics.

allowed: Link an indicator to a canonical place/segment/route only when the official source or an already-verified canonical record proves exact identity.
Use the official inventory as the denominator even when only a subset has canonical Place Registry matches.
Expose relationship coverage such as '13 of 15 public parks matched' as metadata if and only if the unresolved identities are genuinely tracked.
forbidden: Counting Place Registry records to estimate the number of parks, schools, clinics, roads, drains, stops or other citywide infrastructure.
Creating a place relationship from proximity, same barangay or fuzzy name similarity.
Treating a civic-audit target set as a complete city inventory unless its campaign definition explicitly says so.
Creating missing school/health/place records merely to make an indicator relationship appear complete.
placeRegistryRelationshipPolicy.knownExample: The 2023 official public-park denominator is 15, while the current Wave 3 park-accessibility pilot freezes 13 verified public-park targets. These are different scopes until exact source reconciliation proves otherwise.

crossFunctionReuse.use: Current public-school identities, exact health-center/provider identities and other facilities may be surfaced by canonical barangay only when the source identifies the location.
Public parks, health centers, transport facilities and infrastructure segments may receive explicit indicator relationships, but the registry never owns the statistical denominator.
YAKAP/GAMOT provider counts and facility identities can link to health-service guides; service guides keep transaction/eligibility instructions while Statistics owns the dated aggregate.
Infrastructure totals such as drainage or roads can contextualize specific projects, but project spending cannot be treated as proof that aggregate network totals changed.
Land-use composition, public-park coverage, education infrastructure and service-access inventories can support reports through indicator IDs rather than duplicated prose tables.
Use BetterGov/BetterLGU for national or cross-LGU facility/infrastructure comparisons where a canonical resource exists. BetterMakati keeps the local official denominator and primary source visible.
